summary_html: Reports via **state hotlines** (anonymous or confidential). CAPTA conditions funding on operating intake systems with confidentiality and good-faith protections.
authority_html: - **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — intake, confidentiality, immunity, and data requirements tied to federal funding

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: Termination was affirmed on the abandonment ground because the father, who had the Family Court and DCYF addresses and was represented by counsel elsewhere, failed to maintain contact, so the Court did not need to reach the alternative unfitness ground.
key_cases.relevance: The case began with a hotline call describing the incident, illustrating how an anonymous or third-party report opens a DCYF file that can end in termination.
key_cases.quote: Because we are of the opinion that the Family Court justice correctly concluded that respondent abandoned his son, we need not address § 15-7-7(a)(2)(i) as an additional basis for termination.

key_cases.case_name: Curtis v. State Department for Children & Their Families
key_cases.holding: Directed verdicts for a school social worker, a DCF protective worker, a hospital and a physician were affirmed: the school worker was required to report under § 40-11-3, the physician's three-day hospital hold was authorized by § 40-11-5, and no false imprisonment, battery or emotional distress claim was proved.
key_cases.relevance: A report based on second-hand information from teachers was held more than sufficient to mandate a report, which sets a low threshold for hotline intake.
key_cases.quote: Any physical injury apparently caused by other than accidental means is sufficient under § 40-11-5.

mandatory_reporters: Any person (universal mandatory reporting) — R.I. Gen. Laws § 40-11-3(a)
Physicians, certified registered nurse practitioners, and other healthcare providers — additional immediate oral and written report duty, R.I. Gen. Laws § 40-11-6
reporting_details: In Rhode Island any person who has reasonable cause to know or suspect that a child has been abused or neglected must transfer that information to DCYF within 24 hours (R.I. Gen. Laws § 40-11-3(a)).

other: Other abuse or neglect including any action or lack of action which results in harm or potential harm to the physical, mental health, behavioral health or welfare of the child and which is not covered by the other allegations

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediately upon receipt of the report
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in R.I. Gen. Laws § 40-11-3

timeline_requirements.deadline: 30 days, with an extension of up to 15 additional days on supervisor or administrator approval
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in 214-RICR-20-00-1 § 1.9(F), which states that "all efforts are made" to complete each investigation within 30 days
